notes.about: Urdu in the Perso-Arabic script (Naskh code points; how it is drawn, Nastaliq or not, is the app's font). Typed in Latin letters as people chat (Roman Urdu), it gives Urdu words. Written right to left; the engine stores and suggests logical order, as for every script.
notes.letters: Only the letters Urdu words are made of: the Arabic letters Urdu uses (U+0621-U+063A less ة, U+0641-U+0648), and Urdu's own: ٹ پ چ ڈ ڑ ژ ک گ ں ھ ہ ۂ ۃ ی ے ۓ. Arabic's ي ى ك ه and Persian's ۀ are folded to Urdu's by `replace`; Arabic letters Urdu does not use (Sindhi, Pashto, Kashmiri) leave a token out of the lexicon. Digits (U+0660-U+0669, U+06F0-U+06F9), the number signs U+0600-U+0605 and punctuation (، ؛ ؟ ۔ ٪) are not letters of the script, so they split words: a comma written against a word (لیکن،) does not keep it out of the lexicon.
notes.charTable: The same letters, in code point order: Urdu's span U+0621-U+06D3, more than the 128 code points the romanised lexicon and the transliterator used to pack from the script's first (ک is U+06A9, ے U+06D2), so the pack lists them (engine 8).
notes.firstLetter: Any letter but hamza ء, noon ghunna ں and do-chashmi he ھ, which never start a word.
notes.replace: One spelling: Arabic yeh ي and alef maksura ى to Urdu ی, Arabic kaf ك to ک, Arabic heh ه to ہ (gol he), teh marbuta ة to ۃ, Persian ۀ to ۂ; tatweel (kashida) dropped; the short vowels (zabar, zer, pesh), tanween, shadda, sukun and the superscript alef dropped, as everyday Urdu leaves them out and typed Roman Urdu can't say where they were; Arabic-Indic digits to Urdu's. ZWNJ and ZWJ are dropped by the engine's normal form (no `joiners`). Presentation forms (U+FB50-U+FDFF, U+FE70-U+FEFF) are folded to letters by NFKC in data/build-ur-text.sh, before the text reaches the builder.
notes.phraseBreaks: The Urdu full stop ۔ (U+06D4) and question mark ؟ (U+061F) end a sentence.
notes.bases: None: Urdu writes no vowel signs in everyday text, so the keyboard shows no vowel-sign strip.
